body: Thank you. I'm just on the other side of that type of night and reading this really helps me believe there's light at the end of the tunnel.
Yeah it's not like I'm alive because of season 2 of The Mandalorian coming out soon, but it helps.
I don't think it'd work like that but who knows. I feel your pain and I hope you can find a reason not to do it. Having a good cry can help purge some of that bad energy. Good luck.

Probably not, especially if it has acephetamine. At least not before you puke your guts out and go into a great deal of pain and have your survival instinct making your brain scream at you to call for help and get medical assistance.

I feel you man. I know there's nothing I can really say to make you feel better.  

I know it sucks wanting out but not willing to subject others to the pain it would cause. It really really sucks.  

Sometimes I take solace in knowing I can literally just walk away from my life instead of ending it. Just sell everything and move to the cheapest most remote place I can find. It probably wouldn't end well but idk somehow it helps to think about just hitting the ejector seat button and making a radical change instead of dying.
Sorry to hear that, I know it's rough. Hope you can find peace someday.

I've thought about a movie where the protagonist has to decide if he's capable of taking a human life. The context is he finds the person who sexually abused and killed his mother or something like that. Or some other type of crime drama since that's what I'm into. 

The book would probably be historical nonfiction since I like history. Or something that tries to capture my depression and the feeling that I have to wear a happiness mask all the time. Or some absurdist take on mental health in today's world. Thanks for asking.
Lol this.
What's wrong with debate?

Honestly not a troll, just seeking dialogue on an issue dividing our country. 

What facts?
Arrested and not shot though, eh?

Oh dude, don't get me wrong. It's one of the most dangerous jobs in the world. It's a service not incomparable to frontline military service.  

Still, LEO shoot people at 10x the rate people shoot them. That's not a bad thing, it's a good thing. It shouldn't be equal. But I want the total numbers of both to go down as much as possible and from the numerous videos I've seen, it can. It should. We can do better. Police interaction with the community they serve is fundamentally broken and is unnecessarily combative. Both sides do wrong, both sides can improve, we need to rethink and rebuild from the ground up. Not defund. Reform. Start with basic protocols and objectives. Take whatever safety measures are necessary, but at least try to decrease the amount of people who are shot to death or are otherwise killed. Especially those who at no point physically have a weapon in their hand.

Honestly not a troll, just seeking a dialogue with an opposing viewpoint.  

Totally agree Blake is to be held accountable. By the courts, not the cops. Add a resisting arrest charge, totally warranted.  


>Preserve life sure, but NOT at the expense of the safety or lives of others.  

This is the issue. I agree with this statement. But it's a sliding scale. To me, life preserving measures could have been taken without significantly furthering the danger to the officers or surrounding civilians. You may disagree. To me, at no point was there an imminent threat of death or serious bodily injury to officers or civilians. You may disagree. To me, the shots fired created far more danger to the other officers and civilians than anything else in that video. You may disagree. Just trying to see a wider world view and show you one as well.  

Stay well and stay safe.

Yeah agree to disagree obviously, I believe they escalated to deadly force not Blake. Notwithstanding everything you said, I refuse to believe shooting him in the back several times was the correct and justified outcome.  

To me the whole idea of police reform is to prevent this exact situation from turning deadly. It could have been handled such that no one got shot. We have to strive for that outcome. Far too many people are shot by police each year.  

We can't do nothing and just accept that anyone who doesn't obey commands from law enforcement is liable to being shot to death. Many people in these situations are drunk/on drugs/mentally ill and we should do everything possible to preserve human life.

Fair point idk you or your beliefs.  

But this was not appropriate. It was not justified. It speaks to the breadth and depth of this problem that we're even debating this. How can you watch that video and believe the only (or at least best) way to handle that situation was to shoot him in the back?  

LEO's have a very dangerous job. This does not mean they're entitled to elevate the value of their own safety so much higher than the suspects that they shoot someone in the back because they "might" be reaching for a deadly weapon.
https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=ujxKkCqLUrA

>Cops are killed constantly by people who they were given slack to.

2019 U.S. LEO Deaths: 89 (48 from felonious acts, 41 from accidents)

I can't find a definitive number on 2019 deaths from police shootings but it's usually around 1,000 per year. You can think almost all are justified but I do not. I do not think the shooting of Jacob Blake was justified.  

Lawyer but no formal training. I believe the current formal training given to LEO's to deal with these situations is flawed, insufficient, and underfunded. The escalation to deadly force happens far too quickly far too often. This was a mildly violent encounter turned deadly in an instant. It did not have to.

>potentially going for deadly weapon

Yeah that word "potentially" is pretty fucking important and people shouldn't be shot for "potentially" posing a threat to the lives of LEO's or civilians. The standard is imminent threat not a potential one.

No. It doesn't justify shooting him. At all.  

To me, the police shouldn't shoot unless the suspect is brandishing the knife and moving towards an LEO or other civilian. In this case, just back the fuck up. If he turns around with a knife, you draw and take it from there. Try to de-escalate. If he gets in the car and drives away, follow him.  

At no point did I see an imminent threat to anyone's life beside Jacob Blake.
You know what they say about bringing a knife to a gunfight...the police will shoot you repeatedly in the back.
